title: Snoozer Quinn and Jimmy Davis records
summary: He recounts Quinn's records with Jimmy Davis and Davis's singing, then turns to a rant about politicians.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Yeah, he made some things with Jimmy Davis. No, Orrin Blackstone had them. I wouldn't want her. I wouldn't want her. Orrin Blackstone had the records.
I still see some of the Jimmy Davis. I picked up a couple of them. I don't know which ones or whose would be on.

You wouldn't be able to tell he was on them, no, any more than with Whiteman. You can't hear a word. Yeah. I never heard a man hog a thing like Jimmy Davis did. Those things. I mean, you know, most people would give a man like Snoozer a solo because there's a sparkling, terrific beauty there, you see. But no, God Almighty, the man starts singing when the needle drops to cut the record and stops when the record's over.
Boy, what is that, a needle hog or a groove hog, huh? Oh, thank God he can do something, hog a record, huh? He sure can't run a state. And I hope that gets to his ears.
No, he's had so many. Yeah, yeah, he's had so many things.
Got his money. That's all he wants.

Stupid moron. The whole country's run by stupid morons. He's not the only one. No, but... You can't get to be an elected official in this country without being a stupid moron. You'd have to be a stupid moron to run.
